loop.check: Validate dates and required fields; planner compares every condition with the original decision.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per decision; unreadable or ambiguous text returns to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Conditions arrive in varied free text; fixed fields cannot reliably capture their wording and exceptions.

steps.what: Send confirmed restrictions to responsible teams and schedule checks before the event.

tasks.design: Configure a permit register in {WORKFLOW}, linked to event records in {PROJECT} and evidence in {DOCS}, with official {GOV_PORTAL} links, supplier reminders through {EMAIL}, and deterministic application generation. Keep applicability discussions, safety approval, and portal submission with people; a bounded extraction loop drafts permit conditions for review before {WORKFLOW} assigns checks and sends approved instructions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements differ by authority, venue, activity, and existing permissions. Infrequent applications rarely justified bespoke integrations, while evidence collection crossed several organisations.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, document templates, and workflow configuration cover much of the administration. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records and generating applications; bounded extraction can help with varied decision letters.
tasks.still_hard: Confirming which permissions actually apply, assessing technical evidence, and negotiating changes remain demanding. Authority portals may lack interfaces, and inspections depend on external availability.
tasks.human_edge: The planner resolves unclear responsibilities and coordinates practical changes with venue staff, suppliers, and authorities. Competent people remain responsible for safety judgements and declarations.

ambition.what: Early permit readiness checks for small events before venue commitments.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time assembling forms and chasing attachments, and more time resolving venue constraints early. With delegated authority, they can request missing evidence and flag booking holds; safety approval and authority decisions retain their existing owners.

reach.task: Assess event feasibility before approving venue commitments.
reach.learn: Budget approval stages, booking cancellation terms, and how permit lead times affect campaign timing.

reach.task: Evaluate event catering and temporary display arrangements.
reach.learn: How material, waste, and catering choices affect both practical permissions and sustainability requirements.

evidence.claim: Configured checklists, reminders, document generation, and evidence registers can reduce permit administration; the digest supplies no event-permit-specific case.
Venue permissions and responsibility for food service or temporary structures must be checked against applicable local and national rules.
The time shares, remaining effort, and build ranges are planning estimates rather than measured results.
GDPR applies to personal data in applications; consultation requirements depend on national rules and the actual employee-data processing introduced.

assumptions: This is an occasional task in a mid-size European marketing team; venue staff and suppliers provide technical evidence.
Some events use existing venue permissions, so the checklist can close an application path when coverage is confirmed.
Configured official links support retrieval; a person checks current requirements for each unfamiliar authority or event type.
Application generation uses verified fields and attachments, without automatically asserting legal compliance.
The submission channel is represented by {GOV_PORTAL}; some authorities instead require email or paper.
Time shares represent active work, excluding authority processing delays.
Material application amendments repeat the approval step before submission.
Automatic requests and instructions use approved recipients, templates, and confirmed records.
Access estimates include privacy review and any required employee consultation under national rules; they exclude authority permit lead times.
The bounded extraction supports document handling; it does not evaluate workers or make permit decisions.
unknowns: Which jurisdictions, venues, event types, and annual application volumes the team handles.
Which permissions the venues and caterers already hold.
Who can approve declarations, fees, application amendments, and booking holds.
Whether existing {WORKFLOW}, {PROJECT}, and {DOCS} access supports configuration and integration.
Which authority channels the team actually uses.
Whether proposed data handling triggers employee consultation under applicable national rules.
How much current effort goes into repeat applications versus unfamiliar cases.
research_questions: Which official authority handles each activity, and what are its current forms, deadlines, and evidence requirements?
When do existing venue or supplier permissions cover the planned activity?
Which official channels support reusable forms, electronic submissions, or status notifications?
What national rules govern temporary displays, fire safety, food service, and relevant employee consultation?
new_work: Maintain official links, form versions, evidence checklists, and reminder schedules.
Review extracted conditions against original decisions and resolve ambiguous wording.
Handle incomplete supplier evidence and unusual venue requirements.
Check that application changes receive renewed approval when needed.
Maintain access permissions, retention periods, and integration failures.
tasks.statement: Obtain permits from fire and health departments to erect displays and exhibits and serve food at events.

tasks.short: Promote event services through association relationships, brochures and other publications.

steps.what: Collect current service descriptions, capacity, prices and approved event examples.
Prepare an association meeting brief and relevant service examples.

loop.input: Approved service facts, association profile and permitted contact history.
loop.output: An association brief with relevant examples, questions and source references.
loop.check: Validate prices and capacities against source fields; the planner checks relevance and removes unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported tailoring is omitted.
loop.why_not_simpler: Choosing useful discussion points requires reading varied association descriptions and contact notes.

steps.what: Meet association representatives to understand needs and discuss event services.
Draft brochure copy and assemble publication layouts.

loop.input: Approved service facts, audience needs and a fixed publication template.
loop.output: Draft copy in defined sections, rendered into the publication template.
loop.check: Lock prices and capacities to source fields; check claims, required sections, text overflow and accessibility.
loop.stop: One draft and two bounded corrections; unresolved copy or layout issues return to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Layout is deterministic, but audience-specific explanatory copy needs bounded language generation.

steps.what: Review claims, presentation and commercial terms before approving publication.
Publish service material and send approved publications to selected contacts.
Record association needs, follow-up commitments and resulting leads in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: An integration supplies approved service facts from the {DOCS} and contact context from the {CRM}. Bounded drafting loops prepare association briefs and publication copy, deterministic templates render the material, and configured approval and distribution flows connect the {DOCS}, {CMS} and {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relationship knowledge lived with individuals, while publication updates required repeated copying and layout work.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured service facts and reusable templates remove mechanical work. Bounded drafting makes tailored preparation affordable without automating association meetings.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, commercial positioning, publication quality and promises about unusual event requirements still need experienced judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Discover what association representatives need and make credible commitments that fit the relationship.

ambition.what: A small-association event advisory offer

tasks.altitude: The planner can spend more of the week meeting associations and shaping useful service proposals. They can gain authority to recommend standard service bundles within published commercial limits.

reach.task: Maintain a consistent, accessible event-services publication series.
reach.learn: Editorial structure, plain-language editing and publication accessibility.

reach.task: Maintain reusable brochure layouts.
reach.learn: Typography, image permissions and print-ready layout checks.

evidence.claim: Approved facts and fixed layouts support deterministic publication generation, with models used for tailored copy.
Association relationship development remains human work even when preparation and distribution change.

assumptions: This task applies where the company promotes event services to external associations or partners.
A marketing manager approves publication claims and commercial terms.
Distribution uses approved versions and contact lists with applicable suppression rules.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; national rules govern direct marketing and any employee consultation.
Build estimates are working-day effort ranges for a reusable publication and outreach workflow.
unknowns: Whether the company sells event services or only promotes its own events.
Current ownership and accuracy of service descriptions and prices.
Image rights, publication languages and print requirements.
Permitted contact uses and applicable national marketing rules.
research_questions: Which publication formats can use existing templates without custom layout code?
What service scope would make a small-association advisory offer commercially viable?
new_work: Maintain approved service facts, examples and image permissions.
Review generated copy and rendered publications.
Record relationship context and honour follow-up commitments.
Maintain templates, distribution rules and publication expiry dates.
tasks.statement: Promote conference, convention and trades show services by performing tasks such as meeting with professional and trade associations, and producing brochures and other publications.

tasks.short: Develop relevant event topics, select speakers and confirm the programme.

steps.what: Collect audience feedback, event objectives and previous programme material.
Draft topic options and session outlines.

loop.input: Approved programme source pack with source identifiers and event objectives.
loop.output: Topic options with audience needs, session outlines and source references.
loop.check: Require valid source references and separate supported facts from proposed ideas; the planner checks relevance.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing evidence or unresolved claims return to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates structure the options but cannot synthesise varied audience comments into useful themes.

steps.what: Discuss topic relevance, programme balance and audience priorities.
Research speaker credentials and prepare a shortlist.

loop.input: Planner-selected speaker profiles, previous feedback and programme requirements.
loop.output: A comparison of evidenced expertise, topic fit, known fees and missing information.
loop.check: Every factual entry links to a supplied source; unknown fees and availability remain unknown.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unverifiable claims go to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Speaker biographies and feedback are free text with inconsistent descriptions of expertise.

steps.what: Approve speaker choices and outreach spending limits.
Agree speaker participation, fees, availability and session expectations.
Update the programme document with confirmed speakers and sessions.

tasks.design: A deterministic collector assembles an approved source pack from the {DOCS} and {CRM}. Bounded drafting and extraction loops prepare topic options and speaker comparisons, while structured confirmations generate the programme in the {DOCS}; people choose the direction, approve spending and agree participation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Audience feedback and speaker information were scattered and inconsistent, while topic selection depended on context and relationships.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded models can organise supplied text into traceable drafts. Small integrations and document generators are cheaper to implement with AI-assisted coding.
tasks.still_hard: Originality, audience credibility, speaker chemistry and willingness to participate remain difficult to infer from documents.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a programme with a clear point of view and persuade credible speakers to contribute.

ambition.what: A first-time attendee programme track

tasks.altitude: The planner spends more time testing programme ideas with audiences and coaching speakers. With a delegated brief, they can commission sessions for the new attendee track within an approved budget.

reach.role: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
reach.task: Turn audience interviews and feedback into programme priorities.
reach.learn: Interview design, sampling bias and distinguishing demand from isolated comments.

evidence.claim: Source-grounded drafting and extraction can reduce programme preparation without replacing speaker selection.
Structured speaker confirmations can populate programme templates deterministically.

assumptions: The company retains previous programmes and some audience feedback.
Speaker research uses selected sources rather than autonomous web investigation.
Speaker comparisons concern event participation, without inferring sensitive personal traits.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; national rules determine any employee consultation requirements.
Build estimates are working-day effort ranges for one programme workflow.
unknowns: Availability and permitted reuse of feedback and speaker records.
Who approves programme direction, speaker fees and contractual commitments.
Whether the event serves customers, employees or the public.
Required languages and applicable consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Do evidence-linked topic drafts save preparation time while preserving programme originality?
Which speaker criteria can be checked from sources, and which require a conversation?
new_work: Curate the programme source pack and remove stale material.
Verify speaker credentials and factual draft claims.
Maintain comparison fields and programme templates.
Collect audience feedback on the new programme track.
